activities.prompt: Which response defines inflammation?

review.peerReviewedBy: second Codex agent /root/check_inflammation (not Antigravity or Claude)
review.peerReviewNotes: Definition versus regeneration, scarring, emigration and exudation; primary PDF p2. Rebuilt parallel alternatives and item-specific option evidence; rechecked all five against cited original pages. All key/alternative or mapping/order relationships, exact pages, EN/AR meaning, cues and duplicates checked against original page images. No Antigravity or Claude review.

options.text: A dynamic vascularized-tissue response to injury
options.evidence: PDF p2 defines inflammation as the dynamic response of vascularized tissue to injury.

options.text: Replacement of damaged parenchyma by new parenchymal cells
options.evidence: PDF p3 assigns this to regeneration, one route of repair, rather than the definition of inflammation.

options.text: Filling a residual tissue defect with a fibrous scar
options.evidence: PDF p3 assigns this to scar repair, rather than the overall injury response.

options.text: Movement of white cells from microcirculation into tissue
options.evidence: PDF p12 defines the cellular component; it is one component rather than the full response.

options.text: Movement of protein-rich fluid into extravascular tissue
options.evidence: PDF p20 defines exudation, one vascular event rather than the full response.

explanation.en: Inflammation is a dynamic, protective response of vascularized tissue that brings defense and healing mechanisms to injury.
explanation.ar: Inflammation استجابة ديناميكية واقية في النسيج ذي الأوعية، توصل آليات الدفاع والالتئام إلى موضع الأذية.
